title: Marine Acquisition Officer Candidate (I) (Col to 2ndLt) FMOS, MCSC
raw_text:
25. MOS 8057, Marine Acquisition Officer Candidate (I) (Col to 2ndLt) FMOS,
MCSC

    a. Summary. Marine Acquisition Officer Candidates are members of the
acquisition work force. They assist in planning, directing, coordinating,
and supervising specific functional areas that pertain to the acquisition of
aircraft, vehicles, equipment, and weapons. Officers serving in any 8057-
coded billet are required to meet the professional educational standards as
defined by the DoN DAWIA operating guide.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Must be a commissioned officer (limited duty officers are not
eligible (see MOS 8060)).

            (2) Must have 24 months of documented acquisition experience and:

                (a) Life cycle logistics (LCL) functional area.

                (b) Engineering and technical management (ETM).

                (c) Marine Corps Program Management Basic Certification.

                (d) Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA).

            (e) Back to basics (BtB) foundational certified in test &
evaluation (T&E).

            (f) BtB professional certified in contracts (CT) functional area;
or demonstrated progress towards DAWIA BtB practitioner certification in
business financial management (BFM) or business cost estimating (BCE)
functional areas.

       c.   Requirements.   None.

    d. Duties. The Marine Acquisition Officer Candidate participates as a
project officer primarily assigned to provide expertise to a program
management office in highly technical and functional areas that pertain to
the acquisition of equipment and weapon systems.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Purchasing Managers 11-3061.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
